Where things stand

Two web addresses, and neither one shows off the store

Homemakers has two websites today. The old one turns people away with a security warning, and the new one works but looks like thousands of other online shops.

The old address still turns people away

  • Its security certificate ran out on 26 March 2026. Anyone who follows an old link, a business card or a Google result to homemakersseychelles.com is warned that the site "might be trying to steal your information", with a big "Back to safety" button.
  • Behind the warning, the old site has aged. The contact box still holds details from the original template (a New York address), and the footer says © 2022.

homemakers.sc does the job, quietly

  • The range is there. 177 products with good photos, brands and key features. That's a great base to build on.
  • The design is a standard shop layout. It could be any store, anywhere. Nothing on it says Homemakers, and nothing on it gets shared.
  • Your Facebook page has 13,000 followers and new arrivals every week. The website should be a place you're proud to send all of them.
Why a website matters for Homemakers

What a great site does for a home and building store

People in Seychelles plan a build or a new kitchen over weeks, mostly on their phones and mostly in the evening. A website is where that planning can lead to your door.

Open all night

Your store works after 6pm

Customers browse departments, make a list and send it at 10 at night. Your team finds it in the inbox in the morning, ready to price.

Found first

Where people check before they drive

"Hardware store Providence", "tiles Mahé", "is Homemakers open Saturday". A secure, up-to-date site gives Google something good to show, with your hours, directions and phone numbers.

Orders in writing

Lists instead of phone tag

Builders tap what they need (timber sizes, cement, tiles) and email the list to Providence or Victoria with their name and number. Fewer missed calls and fewer "what did they say they wanted?"

Trust

Confidence for bigger purchases

Before spending on a sofa, a bathroom suite or a roof's worth of timber, people check the business looks established. A modern, secure site says you're here, open and serious.

Brands you carry

Show off the names people ask for

Geepas, Cornell, Uyustools, Tramontina, Ariston. When customers can see the brands in each department, they know the trip is worth it.

Two stores, one site

Send people to the right branch

Each store has its own directions, tap-to-call buttons and an "open now / closed" sign that updates itself. Victoria for kitchenware, Providence for the big stuff.

Your own address

Not a listing next to competitors

On directory sites, your page sits beside other hardware stores. On your own site, every click stays with Homemakers.

Works with social

Somewhere to send everyone

Facebook posts, WhatsApp chats and Google Maps can all link to one place that shows the whole store, so every post and conversation has somewhere to lead.

The new site

Scroll and the house builds itself

Homemakers has everything a house needs, from the cement to the cushions. So the site is a house: as you scroll it goes from floor plan to foundations, frame and roof, walls, bathroom, furniture, kitchen and garden. At each stage, gold points open the departments for that part of the build, and every department is its own catalogue page.

The full site is live for you to try. Open it on your phone, scroll through, open a department and make a list. It's on a private preview address and isn't listed on Google.
https://socialmedia-seychelles.github.io/reviews/homemakers-concept/

Open the live site

Every department is a catalogue

Tap a department on the house or in the menu and it opens its own page with every product in it. We've already moved your 177 products over from homemakers.sc, with their photos, brands and key features.

Filters by type (cooking, cooling, bedroom, hand tools…), a search box, and tabs to the other departments at the same stage of the build.

Details, then straight onto the list

Tap any product for a close-up with its key features and whether it's in stock. "Add to list" turns into a quantity counter, so a builder can put 10 of something on the list without leaving the page.

No prices are shown, just like today: the store quotes on request. Departments that aren't online yet, like tiles and mattresses, show the popular items to tap, plus a box for "something else".

The list goes straight to the store

One list follows customers around the whole site, from the house to every department. They add a note ("4 m lengths, delivery to Anse Royale"), pick Providence or Victoria and send. It arrives as a normal email. There's no online payment and nothing for your team to manage: you reply with prices and stock as you do now.

Made to be remembered

Most store websites in Seychelles are a page of text and a contact form. This one is something people show each other. It's the kind of site that gets shared in a WhatsApp group when someone asks "where do I get tiles?"

A clear menu stays at the top the whole time, so anyone in a hurry can skip the house and go straight to a department, the stores or the phone numbers.

On phones, the text sits in a card under the house, with a Menu button and your list always at the top. On older phones that can't show the 3D house, the site switches to a photo version with the same departments and menu.

Questions

Things you might be wondering

We already have homemakers.sc. Why change?

You keep the address and every product. What changes is what people see when they arrive: a site built around Homemakers instead of a template, where a builder can put a whole project on one list and send it to the right branch. We've already moved your catalogue into the concept, so you can see it working.

Do we keep our web addresses?

Yes. The new site goes live on homemakers.sc, and we point the old homemakersseychelles.com at it, so old links and business cards stop showing a warning.

How do new products get added?

We'll agree this on the call. We can add new arrivals for you as they come in, or connect the new design to the product system behind homemakers.sc, so your team keeps adding products the way it does now and they appear on the new site.

Do we have to manage online orders or payments?

No. Customers send a list by email and your team replies with prices and stock, just as you would on the phone. Online payments can be added later if you ever want them.

What if we want something different from the concept?

Tell us on the call. Small changes are free once you buy the site, and anything bigger is quoted before we start, so there are no surprises.

Will it work on older phones?

Yes. Phones that can't show the 3D house get a photo version with the same departments, menu and list.

Who handles other updates later?

Send us changes over WhatsApp or email. We'll talk through an aftercare option on the call so updates are always quick.
